content.title: About
content.content: Tomato Chili Sauce is a spicy condiment made from ripe tomatoes, chili peppers, vinegar and a blend of spices. It delivers a rich tomato flavor with moderate heat and works well as a topping for meat, fish, vegetables, and Asian-inspired dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomato chili sauce is a staple in Mexican and Thai cuisines for adding heat and depth of flavor.
The vitamin C content can provide up to 15 % of the daily value per 100 g, depending on the tomato proportion.
Chili peppers contribute capsaicin, which not only adds spiciness but also a thermogenic effect.
Traditional recipes include vinegar, which extends the product’s shelf life.
The sauce may be smooth or contain chili pieces, depending on the manufacturing process.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes and chilies provide lycopene and vitamin E, which help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Metabolism support
items.content: Capsaicin in chilies can boost metabolism and aid calorie burning.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The sauce contains modest amounts of B6 and folate, important for nervous system function.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: Potassium and magnesium are present, supporting heart and muscle health.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Tomato chili sauce is typically low in fat, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Spicy food sensitivity
items.content: High heat can cause discomfort for people with sensitive stomachs or gastritis.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to tomatoes or the spices used in the sauce.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: The sauce often contains a notable amount of salt; those with hypertension should monitor portions.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Commercial versions may include preservatives that can trigger reactions in sensitive consumers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use tomato chili sauce as a marinade for meat, a topping for burritos, tacos, pizza, pasta, or as a dip for vegetable sticks and shrimp. It can be blended with mayo or sour cream for a milder flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the sauce in a tightly sealed jar in the refrigerator after opening. Unopened, it can be stored at room temperature for up to 12 months. Discard if you notice off‑smell, color changes, or mold growth.
